title: The Lipid-Modulating Effect of Tangeretin on the Inhibition of Angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3) Gene Expression through Regulation of LXRalpha Activation in Hepatic Cells.
authors: Chen, Pei-Yi; Chao, Tzu-Ya; Hsu, Hao-Jen; Wang, Chih-Yang; Lin, Ching-Yen; Gao, Wan-Yun; Wu, Ming-Jiuan; Yen, Jui-Hung
one_liner_zh: 研究柑橘黄酮tangeretin通过调控LXRα转录因子活性抑制ANGPTL3基因表达，涉及TF-DNA调控元件与分子对接，但核心是脂代谢药理而非TF-DNA互作机制建模。
abstract: The excessive accumulation of TG-rich lipoproteins (TGRLs) in plasma is associated with dyslipidemia and atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases (ASCVDs). Tangeretin is a bioactive pentamethoxyflavone mainly found in citrus peels, and it has been reported to protect against hyperlipidemia, diabetes, and obesity. The aim of this study was to investigate the lipid-modulating effects and the underlying mechanisms of tangeretin action in hepatic cells. Transcriptome and bioinformatics analyses with the Gene Ontology (GO) database showed that tangeretin significantly regulated a set of 13 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) associated with the regulation of lipoprotein lipase (LPL) activity. Among these DEGs, angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), an essential inhibitor of LPL catalytic activity that regulates TGRL metabolism in plasma, was markedly downregulated by tangeretin. We demonstrated that tangeretin significantly inhibited the mRNA expression of ANGPTL3 in HepG2 and Huh-7 cells. Tangeretin treatment of hepatic cells also reduced the levels of both intracellular and secreted ANGPTL3 proteins. Moreover, we found that inhibition of ANGPTL3 production by tangeretin augmented LPL activity. We further demonstrated that the transcriptional activity of the ANGPTL3 promoter was significantly attenuated by tangeretin, and we identified a DNA element located between the -250 and -121 positions that responded to tangeretin. Furthermore, we found that tangeretin did not alter the levels of the nuclear liver X receptor alpha (LXRalpha) protein, an essential transcription factor that binds to the tangeretin-responsive element, but it can counteract LXRalpha-mediated ANGPTL3 transcription. On the basis of molecular docking analysis, tangeretin was predicted to bind to the ligand-binding domain of LXRalpha, which would result in suppression of LXRalpha activation. Our findings support the hypothesis that tangeretin exerts a lipid-lowering effect by modulating the LXRalpha-ANGPTL3-LPL pathway, and thus, it can be used as a potential phytochemical for the prevention or treatment of dyslipidemia.
abstract_zh: 血浆中富含甘油三酯的脂蛋白（TGRLs）的过度积累与血脂异常和动脉粥样硬化性心血管疾病（ASCVDs）相关。橘皮素（Tangeretin）是一种主要存在于柑橘果皮中的生物活性五甲氧基黄酮，已有报道称其对高脂血症、糖尿病和肥胖具有保护作用。本研究旨在探讨橘皮素在肝细胞中的脂质调节作用及其潜在机制。通过转录组学和生物信息学分析，结合基因本体论（GO）数据库，发现橘皮素显著调控了一组与脂蛋白脂肪酶（LPL）活性调节相关的13个差异表达基因（DEGs）。在这些DEGs中，血管生成素样蛋白3（ANGPTL3）——一种抑制LPL催化活性并调节血浆中TGRL代谢的关键抑制剂——被橘皮素显著下调。我们证明，橘皮素在HepG2和Huh-7细胞中显著抑制了ANGPTL3的mRNA表达。橘皮素处理肝细胞还降低了细胞内和分泌型ANGPTL3蛋白的水平。此外，我们发现橘皮素抑制ANGPTL3的产生增强了LPL活性。我们进一步证明，橘皮素显著减弱了ANGPTL3启动子的转录活性，并鉴定了一个位于-250至-121位置之间的DNA元件对橘皮素产生响应。此外，我们发现橘皮素并未改变核内肝X受体α（LXRalpha）蛋白的水平——该蛋白是结合橘皮素响应元件的关键转录因子——但它能抵消LXRalpha介导的ANGPTL3转录。基于分子对接分析，预测橘皮素可结合LXRalpha的配体结合域，从而抑制LXRalpha的激活。我们的研究结果支持以下假设：橘皮素通过调节LXRalpha-ANGPTL3-LPL通路发挥降脂作用，因此，它可作为预防或治疗血脂异常的潜在植物化学物质。
